summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with chronic pancreatitis, type 2 diabetes, and hypertension was admitted after presenting with worsening abdominal pain due to running out of his home morphine. He developed hypoglycemia during a clinic visit and was found to have elevated white blood cell count, consistent with inflammation from a pancreatitis flare. He was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and IV pain control. His pain improved within 24 hours, and he transitioned to oral intake and his baseline oral pain regimen. A single episode of hematuria was noted but did not recur; urine culture showed no infection, and imaging revealed stable chronic pancreatitis with benign renal cysts. He was discharged home in stable condition with no medication changes except for the addition of aspirin and short-term pain medication supply, with instructions to follow up with his primary care provider.
